text:
sara_support: FYI customer CS-4827 reporting spikes of 504s and long tail latency for hosted inference since ~09:10 UTC. support ticket: https://redwood.support/t/CS-4827 :frowning:
alex_oncall: on it. which model + region? any recent deploys? :eyes:
mike_runtime: saw same alerts in perf dashboards — continuous-batching backlog jumped and queue depth hit 5000 for hostpool us-west-2 around 09:09. model = opt-30b-qat, seq len ~128, lots of short requests (10-30 tokens).
sara_support: tenant: foodly-prod, region: us-west-2. customer says it began after autoscale window this morning. they included request id 7f4a2c1e-9b3a in ticket with 504.
alex_oncall: deploy-bot shows a canary completed at 08:58 for runtime 6.2.2 -> 6.2.3. @deploy-bot can you paste the rollout note?
deploy-bot: Canary rollout 6.2.3 -> success (canary 3/3) at 08:58 UTC. No immediate errors reported on deploy channel. :white_check_mark:
mike_runtime: quick triage: batching efficiency tanked after scale-in. Many short requests cause small batches so per-token overhead increases and KV cache misses spike when new workers cold-start. GPU utilization low but queue depth growth causes dequeue latencies -> gateway times out at 30s.
nisha_infra: infra metrics: enqueue rate for foodly-prod surged ~3x from 09:05-09:12; autoscaler removed one node at 09:03 (scale-in). That combination looks like a classic cold-start + packing inefficiency.
sara_support: customer impacted ~3% of requests 504s, p95 jumped from 120ms -> 9.8s. They're asking for root cause and a mitigation asap.
alex_oncall: mitigation ideas — 1) throttle tenant at edge to steady rate, 2) temporarily pin tenant to dedicated pool, 3) rollback runtime 6.2.3 -> 6.2.2 if canary introduced a scheduling change. Which is fastest?
mike_runtime: fastest = throttle at edge for foodly-prod (add token bucket limit), then bump queue depth limit and disable continuous batching for that tenant so requests go direct (reduces batching overhead). I can push a temporary routing override. Also instrument KV cache warmup hook.
nisha_infra: I can pause autoscaler for the pool and force one extra node for 10m to absorb burst.
sara_support: I'll tell customer we're throttling to safe rate and working on warmup. updating ticket and CS.
alex_oncall: mike, please add the routing override + disable continuous batching for tenant and paste the commands you ran.
mike_runtime: ran:
```
# routing override
redwoodctl route override --tenant foodly-prod --pool hosted-usw2-batch --policy direct
# disable continuous batching for tenant
redwoodctl tenant update --id foodly-prod --continuous_batching false
```
applied at 09:28 UTC. monitoring now.
nisha_infra: spun up +1 node and paused autoscaler at 09:29. node ready 09:33.
alex_oncall: metrics update?
mike_runtime: within 2m after overrides p95 dropped to 340ms, queue depth decreased and 504s gone for new requests. still rolling through backlog but customer CC says errors stopped.
sara_support: customer confirms success, thanks team. I'll leave ticket open for RCA and follow-up action (autoscaler guardrails + batching heuristics).
alex_oncall: RCA notes to capture: interaction of scale-in during burst of short-lived requests -> poor packing -> KV cache thrash -> queue saturation -> gateway 30s timeout. Action items: add scale-in cooldown when enqueue rate > X, add tenant-aware batching config, expose tenant-level throttle, improve observability for KV cache cold starts.
mike_runtime: filing a GH issue with traces + logs: https://github.com/redwood-infra/issues/4521
sara_support: good. closing slack thread when ticket updated. :thumbsup:
